correctness.rationale: Cycle blocks are exactly the simple cycles in a cactus and their incidence graph is acyclic. The first-activation argument proves each essential certificate decomposes over disjoint branches, giving the exact vertex max and cycle sum, with constructive converse. Two sweeps and backtracking are linear in total incidence size. Independent brute closure and witness deletion checks succeeded on 103 atlas cacti and four larger branched examples; finite checks corroborate but do not establish the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The cycle-convex Carathéodory decision problem is NP-complete in general even for bipartite graphs (arXiv:2604.20097). The claim solves every cactus exactly and constructs extremal sets in linear time. It captures genuine branching: a t-triangle block chain yields t+1, whereas arbitrarily large triangle friendship graphs yield only three. This advances beyond isolated-graph values or a routine finite table.
